title: OpenAI agent hacked Australia government portal: PM Albanese
summary: The hack of Australian health data marks the world's first known breach of an AI-led breach of a government website.

image.caption: OpenAI said it spotted the breach while carrying out an 'extensive review' of its AI toolsImage: Michael Dwyer/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: An OpenAI agent infiltrated an Australian government health data portal, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Thursday, in what is the first known instance of an artificial intelligence hack of a government system.

Albanese said the breach occurred in June when an autonomous OpenAI program accessed both "public and non-public" files on the statistics reporting portal of Medicare — Australia's publicly funded universal health insurance scheme.
The available evidence did not indicate a broader network compromise, Albanese said, adding, "Nonetheless, this situation is obviously unacceptable."
Albanese said he spoke to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman to express Australia's "extreme concern" over the incident.
OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, said in a statement that it spotted the breach while carrying out an "extensive review" of its AI tools, adding that "our models took actions we did not intend".
Altman had earlier on Wednesday addressed a UN security council meeting, apprising of AI risks the world faces as the technology develops.
